final_message:
I've written the draft Bluebird Bakery trends report for September 2026, with eight commentary bullets for the reviewer. The script calculated every figure; I only wrote the commentary.

**Data quality:** one mismatch. In Mar 2026, "Total for Professional Services" says 2,225.00, but its line items add up to 2,200.00 (25.00 apart). The analysis uses the line items, and the reviewer decides which figure is right; the commentary opens with this. Two other parts of the sheet's layout had to be rebuilt:
- "Total Delivery" had no heading row, so it was matched to the two lines above it.
- "Charitable Donations" has no values and no total row, so it was treated as a blank account.

The other cross-checks pass (gross profit, net income, and the balance sheet balancing). The export covers only 9 months (Jan–Sep 2026), so trailing-twelve-month and year-over-year comparisons aren't available, and the commentary says so.

**Main points:**
- **Revenue:** 81,300, the highest month in the export. That's up 17.7% on August and 17.3% above the prior six-month average. It includes 12,000 from a new "Wholesale Accounts" stream, which is zero in every earlier month; the reviewer should confirm whether it will continue. Bread Sales keeps rising and Pastry Sales keeps falling.
- **Gross margin:** 65.3%, up 5.7 points on August and the best month in the period.
- **Costs:** operating expenses rose 21.0% to 31,570, mostly because Wages & Salaries went from a flat 16,000 to 21,000. Mystery Shopper Program shows as "from 0" against August, but it was also 400 in March and June. I described it as recurring every third month, not as a new line.
- **Cash:** the bank balance is 37,600, down 1,800 on August and 10,800 on six months earlier, even though net income (21,553) was positive in every month. I left the reason as a question for the reviewer.

**Accounts that fell into "Other":** Instagram Ads, Mystery Shopper Program and Supplier Rebates matched no category rule.
